executive_assessment.text: Child-risk mapping differentiates six high-risk wilayas, while Hodh El Chargui and Mbera-area evidence adds drought, displacement and service/resource pressures.
DPPA identifies mediated grazing/water and transhumance tensions, alongside committees and policy capacities; these are qualitative pathways, not national causal estimates.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-09-26 reports: Outside Mbera, the study reports host-refugee grazing competition and possible water-access discord across refugee arrival cohorts.

Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF rates child climate exposure and vulnerability high or very high in 11 wilayas; six highest-risk are Hodh El Chargui, Gorgol, Hodh El Gharbi, Guidimakha, Tagant and Assaba; poorest, least-served children face greatest risks.
Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF estimates about half of Hodh El Chargui communities face severe or high drought risk.
Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF reports 2022 flood damage in Tagant, Assaba and Hodh El Gharbi; it warns flood displacement can expose children to violence, exploitation and trafficking.
Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: As of 30 June 2024, Mbera hosted 108,059 registered refugees; women and children were 83% of camp registrants.

Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports Mali's humanitarian-security crisis drove arrivals into Hodh Chargui, with camp saturation sending many to neighboring villages and straining services and natural resources in a poor, climate-shock-vulnerable region.
Source dated 2024-08-02 reports: UNHCR reports monthly arrival monitoring in over 60 villages and an area-based response with partners and local authorities for refugees and host communities.
Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: By end-August 2025, rainfall deficits persisted in Hodh Ech Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi; dry spells and floods caused localized crop losses.

Source dated 2025-09-09 reports: For June-August 2025, FAO reports about 44,000 refugees in Hodh Ech Chargui faced acute food insecurity, including over 6,000 in Phase 4; 17% of resident Mauritanians needed aid.

known_gaps.text: Mauritania’s 2025 NDC 3.0 PDF was not readable through the available web reader, so no claims are taken from it.
The reviewed country sources do not establish a Mauritania-specific climate-conflict pathway; none is asserted here.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
No inspected source establishes climate as a cause of armed violence in Mauritania; DPPA presents plausible pathways, not causal estimates or incident-level mapping.
Only the 3-page DPPA executive summary was accessible, not the underlying longer study; its geographic detail and evidence limits should be retained.
The UNICEF report's risk scores concern children and climate exposure/vulnerability, not FCV; the report carries 2024 copyright and should not be read as a 2026 update.
UNHCR 2024 and FAO 2025 population and food-security figures are dated snapshots; this extraction does not verify 2026 values.
The official UNHCR May 2025 environment and climate factsheet download returned an error page and its indexed text was excluded from evidence.

Main inspected the three-page DPPA executive summary and other primary publications. Cohort representation, longstanding resentments and resource governance mediate risks; refugee presence is not itself a violence predictor.
The UNICEF composite is a child climate-risk measure, not an FCV classification; the report's dated baselines and historical assistance figures are retained.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
